Find and Browse Count Table Ordination Methods

Source: R/count_ord.r
count_ords.Rd

Programmatic access to the list of ordination methods that count_ord() runs, and their associated functions.

Usage

list_count_ords(
  val = c("data.frame", "list", "func", "id", "name"),
  nm = c(NA, "id", "name")
)

match_count_ord(method)

Arguments

val

Sets the return value for this function call. See "Value" section below. Default: "data.frame"

nm

What value to use for the names of the returned object. Default is "id" when val is "list" or "func", otherwise the default is NA (no name).

method

The name of an ordination method to search for. Supports partial matching. All non-alpha characters are ignored.

Value

match_count_ord()

A list with the following elements.

  • name : Method name, e.g. "Principal Component Analysis"

  • id : Method ID - also the name of the function, e.g. "pca"

  • func : The function for this method, e.g. ecodive::pca

  • params : Formal args for func, e.g. c("counts", "margin", ...)

list_count_ords()

The returned object's type and values are controlled with the val and nm arguments.

  • val = "data.frame" : The data.frame from which the below options are sourced.

  • val = "list" : A list of objects as returned by match_count_ord() (above).

  • val = "func" : A list of functions.

  • val = "id" : A character vector of method IDs.

  • val = "name" : A character vector of method names.

If nm is set, then the names of the vector or list will be the method ID (nm="id") or name (nm="name"). When val="data.frame", the names will be applied to the rownames() property of the data.frame.

Examples


    # A data.frame of all available methods.
    list_count_ords()
#>                                                      name         id
#> 1                                 Correspondence Analysis         ca
#> 2                       Canonical Correspondence Analysis        cca
#> 3                    Double Principal Coordinate Analysis      dpcoa
#> 4                            Linear Discriminant Analysis        lda
#> 5  Orthogonal Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis     oplsda
#> 6                            Principal Component Analysis        pca
#> 7             Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis      plsda
#> 8                                     Redundancy Analysis        rda
#> 9                                    Robust Aitchison PCA       rpca
#> 10                      Phylogenetic Robust Aitchison PCA rpca_phylo

    # Find the method for 'prcomp'.
    m <- match_count_ord('prcomp')
    m$id
#> [1] "pca"
